shardDecision: 16 files / 508 changed lines, but the files they live in run to 4,400 lines of code plus a 1,500-line spec bundle that itself moved this pass — more than one context should hold if every file is to be read in full. Split two ways along the boundary the change has: shard 1 took the web, validation and e2e side (6 files, 269 changed lines) and shard 2 the API and the spec documents (10 files, 239 changed lines). I held the three a child cannot do — the requirement sweep, the boundary sweep and blast radius — and checked all three of pass 1's blockers against their witnesses myself as well as through the shards.

priorBlockers.why: The contradiction is gone from the documents and the code implements the side they settled on. REQ-01-036 (specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md:370), REQ-01-051 (:380), contracts §Routes rows 12 and 14, the Error Messages table (contracts.md:177) and Validation Rule 9 (contracts.md:238) now all say one thing: empty, or two uppercase letters naming an assigned country, refused with PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid at 422 on the organization write and 400 on the member write. Edge case 10 (contracts.md:395) was amended to agree — XX 'cannot come from the write either'. `git grep countryCodeInvalid -- specs` returns only the two prose lines explaining why it is NOT the message here. The code follows: organization-country.service.ts:76 and the wantsCountry branch at members.service.ts:457 both call validateStatedCountryCode (packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts:248), which runs the /^[A-Z]{2}$/ shape test and then validateCountryCode's membership test of COUNTRY_NAMES, so 'pl' and 'XX' are both refused with 'Enter a valid country'. TC-01-INT-21 and TC-01-INT-25 loop over 'XX' and assert the stored value is unchanged. What the settlement did NOT reach is the picker that feeds both writes — L1 below.

todayISO() is deleted. The initial anchor (CalendarScreen.tsx:138) and the calendar-today control (:300) both call timeOffCalendarToday(session.account.timezone), and the endpoint now calls the same two helpers for range.today instead of its own private copies — the diff at apps/api/src/time-off/time-off-calendar.service.ts deletes resolveTimezone and todayIn and imports resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone and timeOffCalendarToday. One field, one function, so the Kiritimati scenario in the witness now puts the anchor and the marker on the same day. session.account.timezone is `string | null` on the session context (apps/web/src/layout/session-context.tsx:10), the same field the API reads, and the helper falls back to UTC for null, empty and unrecognized zones, which is REQ-01-018's own fallback. Residue is a note: the helper restates todayInTimeZone, which already ships and which the handoff named (S1-N1).

The thrown-fetch branch at CalendarScreen.tsx:243 no longer draws TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.emptyStateBody; it draws HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError, a packages/validation export, and emptyStateBody is now reached only from the empty-state block the contracts assign it to. A neighbouring path on the same statement is still wrong, but it is not F3's: a non-ok response whose body carries `message` and no `fields` echoes the framework's own string into the banner (S1-2).

findings.rule: sweep 9 — a client rule and its server re-check must agree; contracts §Screens pins the option list ('It is the country picker the holiday form already uses', contracts.md:337) while §Validation Rules rule 9 refuses part of what that list offers
findings.claim: the settled write rule refuses three codes the picker the same document names still offers, so an admin can select Kosovo (or Ascension Island, or Tristan da Cunha) from either country picker and be refused with 'Enter a valid country' — and a holiday row for the same code can already be created, so the two halves of the holiday feature disagree about which countries exist

witness.detail: An admin opens Settings > Holidays and picks the option whose value is 'XK' from org-country-select, then presses org-country-save. The screen sends PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with {"countryCode":"XK"} (page.tsx:166). validateStatedCountryCode passes the shape test and then fails validateCountryCode, because COUNTRY_NAMES holds only officially assigned alpha-2 codes (autofill.ts:686, and its comment: 'All 249 officially assigned codes'), so the API answers 422 {"fields":{"countryCode":"Enter a valid country"}} about a value the product itself offered. The same three options are on member-country-select, which is MEMBER_COUNTRY_OPTIONS = the default option + HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS (MemberDetailScreen.tsx:42-44, drawn at :336), refused there with 400. Command that settles which codes: `node -e "const {getCountries,getCountryCallingCode}=require('libphonenumber-js'); ..."` comparing the picker's source list against the COUNTRY_NAMES keys parsed out of autofill.ts prints `COUNTRY_NAMES size 249 / phone list size 245 / in picker but NOT assigned: AC,TA,XK`. HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS takes its codes from COUNTRY_OPTIONS, the phone picker's list (country-options.ts:20; apps/web/src/account-data.ts builds it from libphonenumber's getCountries()), and labels them through countryName(), which returns the bare code for an unknown one — so the three appear as options labelled 'AC', 'TA' and 'XK'. The document requires both halves and they cannot both hold: contracts.md:337 pins the organization picker to the holiday form's picker and :345-347 pins the member's to the same list with one option above it, while rule 9 (:238) and REQ-01-036 / REQ-01-051 refuse anything outside the assigned list. Which side gives is a product decision, not an implementation one: the holiday create route still accepts 'XK' (validateHolidayCountryCode is shape-only, holidays.ts:101), so an organization can hold a holiday row for a country no member and no organization may ever be set to — narrowing the picker strands those rows, and widening the write reinstates exactly the silent discard the settlement was written to stop.

findings.suggestedFix: a person decides and writes it into the document: either the two country pickers draw from the assigned list (and the document says so, and says what happens to a holiday row already carrying an unassigned code), or rule 9 accepts the picker's list and REQ-01-026's read is stated to discard the rest. Not settled by the reviewer and not by the implementer — both readings are written down and each costs something different.

findings.rule: sweep 9 — a message and its table: contracts §Error Messages is the closed set of what this screen may say, and handoff T7(b) states the rule in full
findings.claim: on a non-ok response whose body carries `message` but no `fields`, calendar-error-banner draws the server's raw framework string — a message no packages/validation export holds and the contracts' Error Messages table gives no row

witness.detail: A caller has the calendar open and their capability is revoked, or the API restarts. The next range step issues GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar and Nest answers 404 {"message":"Not Found","statusCode":404}; a 500 answers {"message":"Internal server error","statusCode":500}. Line 234 evaluates `fields ? Object.values(fields)[0] : (body?.message ?? HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError)`: fields is undefined and body.message is present, so calendar-error-banner renders 'Not Found' or 'Internal server error' to the reader. Neither string exists in packages/validation and neither is in specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.contracts.md §Error Messages (lines 164-179), whose only rows for this route are the seven TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES 422 messages. The plan states the rule verbatim in handoff.json T7 (b): 'Only a 422 carrying fields draws the endpoint's own message (the first value of fields); every other outcome draws the generic one, which also keeps a raw framework string such as "Internal server error" off the screen.' The generic branch is already written on the same line, so the fallback chain is one term too long. Verified by reading the file at HEAD; this line changed in this pass's fix commit, which added the toastServerError tail and kept the body.message term ahead of it.

findings.suggestedFix: setError(fields ? Object.values(fields)[0] : HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError) — never echo the response's own message

findings.rule: sweep 8 — a test that fails for a reason other than the rule it guards
findings.symbol: picking four people holds through every window preset and step
findings.claim: the new week-start assertion computes the expected Monday from the runner's UTC clock while the screen computes its anchor in the account's Europe/Berlin zone — the browser-clock/account-zone split F2 was raised about, reintroduced inside the assertion that guards it

witness.detail: signupOrg seeds the account with timezone 'Europe/Berlin' (e2e/tests/helpers.ts:138). The screen's anchor is timeOffCalendarToday('Europe/Berlin'); the test takes new Date() at line 279, reduces it to the runner's UTC calendar date and steps back to that date's Monday. On a Sunday between 22:00 and 23:59 UTC under CEST the account is already on Monday while the runner is still on Sunday, so the screen renders the week beginning that Monday and the assertion expects calendar-day-header-<previous Monday>: the case fails against correct code. Nothing else in the case is time-dependent — the day-header counts at 274 and 277 hold in every zone.

findings.suggestedFix: derive the expected Monday from the account's zone the way the screen does, or assert the first header's weekday label rather than its date

findings.rule: contracts §UI Description, Loading — 'The grid area holds a skeleton of the header rows plus six member rows'
findings.claim: the skeleton is not drawn in the grid's own geometry: in the only state that renders it, the column template it is handed declares one day column while it places fourteen

witness.detail: The skeleton renders only under `loading && !data` (line 385). gridColumns is computed at line 258 from `days = data?.days ?? []`, so with data null it is `var(--name-col) repeat(1, minmax(0, 1fr))`. GridSkeleton then places cells at gridColumn 2 through 15, creating thirteen implicit auto-sized tracks; the placeholders inside them are width: 100% (globals.css:1115), which in an auto track resolves against no definite width. findings.suggestedFix: give the skeleton its own template of fourteen columns rather than the data-derived gridColumns

dismissed.concern: what is this change for, and what would make it wrong in a way none of the above catches
dismissed.why: It is a read-only wallchart plus a chain that decides which holidays a member is paid for, and the second half is where money moves. I looked specifically for a way the chain can be right at every call site and still pay the wrong person: the four adoptions are all present and no phone read survives; the read is deliberately forgiving and the write deliberately strict; the fixtures now discriminate between the old source and the new. What I found instead is the one place where strict-write and shipped-picker meet and disagree (L1), and its consequence is exactly of that kind — an admin who cannot state the country their people are paid holidays for, told it is not a valid country.
